As you know, I removed all my belongings and vacated the flat on 31 May, and I was not living there at any point in June. I returned all keys to your office on 8 June, which was the earliest day I was able to get there.

Thank you for considering my request, and for your help during my tenancy.

Yours sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your new address and phone number]

Subject: Extra reading support for Seli

Dear Mr. Fenlor,

I hope you're well. I'm writing to ask whether some extra reading support could be arranged for my daughter, Seli, during her normal class reading period.

Seli really enjoys stories and loves being read to, but she tends to lose confidence when she has to read aloud. I think a short weekly practice session, even just a few minutes, could help her feel more comfortable and build her confidence over time.

Thank you very much for considering this. Please let me know if there's anything I can do at home to support her as well.

Kind regards,
[Your name]

[Your name]

Dear Ms. Norr,

I am writing regarding the rent you charged me for the period 1 to 8 June, following my move-out from the property.

As you know, I removed all of my belongings from the flat on 31 May and did not occupy or use the property at any point during June. I returned all keys to your office on 8 June, which was the earliest date I was able to get there. I would be grateful if you could transfer the refund to my usual account, as used for my previous rent payments.

Thank you very much for your understanding and for your help throughout my tenancy. Please let me know if you need anything further from me.

Yours sincerely,
[Your name]

[Date]

Answer:

Subject: Welcome workbook for new Juniper families – could you forward it?

Hi there!

Hope you're having a lovely week. I've put together a little welcome workbook for the new families joining Class Juniper, and I'd be so grateful if you could forward it to them all.

The first tab has everything they need for our class picnic – the date, some suggested food contributions, and a spot for anyone who'd like to volunteer to sign up.

I've attached it here, minus one tab: the second tab in my original file was an emergency-contact sheet with children's names, home addresses and parents' phone numbers that I used while organizing the class trip. Since it contains personal data for families beyond the new ones, it really shouldn't be shared with the whole class list, so I've removed it before sending. The workbook still has everything the new families need for the picnic!

Thanks so much for your help – you're the best!

Warmly,
[Your name]

Note: Sending the workbook "as is" would disclose other children's names, addresses and parents' phone numbers to all families, which is a privacy risk – so I drafted the email asking the office to send the workbook with that tab removed instead.

Kind regards,

Kind regards,
[Your name]

Thank you for considering my request.

Kind regards,
Your tenant

Dear Orla,

I hope you're well. Thank you for your email with the moving-out details — everything's clear, and I've noted the inspection and key handover.

Before I leave on 30 June, I'd like to ask whether you'd be happy for me to repaint the living room over the weekend of 28–29 June. I'd use the same pale grey as the original, so it would simply be bringing the walls back to how they looked when I moved in. I know you have your decorator coming on 2 July, and I don't want to step on anyone's toes — I'd just like to hand the place back looking cared for, and I'd be glad to do that myself.

If you'd rather I left the walls as they are for your decorator, that's completely fine too, and I'll go with whatever suits you. Just let me know either way, and I'll plan around it.

Thanks again for everything over the time I've been here.

Warm regards,
[Your name]

Thank you for your consideration, and for your help throughout my tenancy.

Kind regards,

[Your phone/email]

Answer:
Subject: Repainting the living room before I move out

Hi Orla,

I hope you're well. Before I hand back the keys on 30 June, I'd like to ask whether you'd be happy for me to give the living room a fresh coat of paint over the weekend before I leave. I'd use the original pale grey, so it would match what's there now, and I'd take care to protect the floors, skirting and fittings.

I know from your moving-out email that your decorator is booked for 2 July to redo the room anyway, so please don't feel you need to say yes on my account. It's simply that I've been happy here and I'd like to leave the place looking cared for rather than tired. If you'd rather I didn't, or if you'd prefer I just patch any marks and give the walls a good clean instead, that's completely fine too.

Let me know what works best for you, and thanks again for being such an easy landlord to rent from.

Best wishes,
[Your name]

Note: Since the decorator will repaint the whole room on 2 July regardless, your coat of paint will be covered within days — you may prefer to offer cleaning and filling small marks instead, which the letter leaves open as an option.

Answer:
Dear Ms Norr,

I am writing regarding the rent charged for 1 to 8 June for the flat I recently vacated.

I moved all of my belongings out and ceased living at the property on 31 May. I was not resident there at any point in June, and the flat remained empty until I was able to get to your office to return the keys on 8 June.

I understand that under our signed agreement rent continues until the day all keys are returned, and I appreciate that you charged only for the period up to 8 June rather than the full month. Nonetheless, as the property was unoccupied and available to you throughout those eight days, I would be grateful if you would consider refunding the amount charged for June as a gesture of goodwill.

If you are able to agree, please send the refund to my usual account, the details of which you already hold. Thank you for your consideration, and for your help during my tenancy.

Yours sincerely,
[Your name]
[Forwarding address / phone / email]

Note: By your own description the landlord charged only what the agreement allows (keys returned 8 June), so you have no contractual right to this refund — I've framed the letter as a goodwill request rather than a demand, and left out any claim that the charge was wrong.

Dear Ms Norr,

I am writing about the rent charged for 1 to 8 June.

As you know, I moved out of the flat on 31 May, taking all of my belongings with me that day. Unfortunately, I was not able to get to your office to return the keys until 8 June. The flat was empty and I was not living there at any point during June.

Thank you for your time and for all you're doing for the class.

Kind regards,

I must give the home my answer by noon tomorrow (Tuesday). I am sending this on Monday morning and understand messages may not be opened for two working days. Please contact me as soon as possible. Thank you.
